name: IoT & Embedded Security
description: Security of IoT devices, embedded systems, firmware, and smart-home ecosystems.
narrative:
The earliest USENIX Security work in this area (2018) reflected an explosion of consumer IoT and the realization that these devices broke old security assumptions. Several threads opened at once: physical-world abuse of cyber-attacks, as in "BlackIoT: IoT Botnet of High Wattage Devices Can Disrupt the Power Grid" (2018), which showed a botnet of air conditioners could destabilize the grid; voice-assistant security, with "Skill Squatting Attacks on Amazon Alexa" (2018) and "CommanderSong: A Systematic Approach for Practical Adversarial Voice Recognition" (2018); and the human side of smart homes, with "Rethinking Access Control and Authentication for the Home Internet of Things (IoT)" (2018). At the same time researchers began grappling with the hard problem of analyzing the firmware itself, since IoT software is full of bare-metal, hard-to-emulate code — "Inception: System-Wide Security Testing of Real-World Embedded Systems Software" (2018) and "ACES: Automatic Compartments for Embedded Systems" (2018) tackled testing and isolation on these constrained targets.

Around 2019-2020 the field's center of gravity shifted toward two practical engineering challenges: scaling automated firmware analysis, and measuring the real-world IoT ecosystem. "FIRM-AFL: High-Throughput Greybox Fuzzing of IoT Firmware via Augmented Process Emulation" (2019) made fuzzing IoT firmware fast enough to be useful, and "HALucinator: Firmware Re-hosting Through Abstraction Layer Emulation" (2020) cracked the re-hosting problem by emulating hardware abstraction layers so firmware could run off-device. On the measurement side, "All Things Considered: An Analysis of IoT Devices on Home Networks" (2019) gave the first large-scale empirical picture of what devices people actually run. This period also matured the physical-injection attack genre with "Light Commands: Laser-Based Audio Injection Attacks on Voice-Controllable Systems" (2020), which used lasers to silently command assistants.

By 2021-2022 the work became more targeted and systematic. Firmware rehosting and bug-finding kept advancing — "Jetset: Targeted Firmware Rehosting for Embedded Systems" (2021), "Sharing More and Checking Less: Leveraging Common Input Keywords to Detect Bugs in Embedded Systems" (2021), and "Fuzzware: Using Precise MMIO Modeling for Effective Firmware Fuzzing" (2022) pushed emulation and fuzzing toward precise hardware modeling. In parallel the community turned to defending deployed smart homes and understanding IoT threats in the wild: "HAWatcher: Semantics-Aware Anomaly Detection for Appified Smart Homes" (2021) brought semantics-aware anomaly detection, "The Circle Of Life: A Large-Scale Study of The IoT Malware Lifecycle" (2021) characterized the post-Mirai malware ecosystem, and "Lumos: Identifying and Localizing Diverse Hidden IoT Devices in an Unfamiliar Environment" (2022) addressed the emerging privacy threat of hidden snooping devices. The arc runs from "these devices can hurt the physical world" toward robust tooling to analyze firmware at scale and practical defenses for the messy, multi-user, real-world IoT ecosystem.

milestones.title: BlackIoT: IoT Botnet of High Wattage Devices Can Disrupt the Power Grid
milestones.note: framed IoT as a physical-world threat, showing compromised high-wattage devices could destabilize the power grid

milestones.title: Rethinking Access Control and Authentication for the Home Internet of Things (IoT)
milestones.note: reframed smart-home security around multi-user, real-world access-control needs rather than single-device assumptions

milestones.title: FIRM-AFL: High-Throughput Greybox Fuzzing of IoT Firmware via Augmented Process Emulation
milestones.note: made greybox fuzzing of IoT firmware fast enough to be practical, seeding a wave of firmware-analysis tooling

milestones.title: All Things Considered: An Analysis of IoT Devices on Home Networks
milestones.note: delivered the first large-scale empirical measurement of IoT devices actually deployed in real homes

milestones.title: HALucinator: Firmware Re-hosting Through Abstraction Layer Emulation
milestones.note: solved firmware re-hosting via HAL emulation, letting embedded firmware run and be analyzed off-device

milestones.title: HAWatcher: Semantics-Aware Anomaly Detection for Appified Smart Homes
milestones.note: advanced runtime defense with semantics-aware anomaly detection for automated smart homes

milestones.title: The Circle Of Life: A Large-Scale Study of The IoT Malware Lifecycle
milestones.note: characterized the full post-Mirai IoT malware lifecycle, exposing gaps in current defenses

milestones.title: Fuzzware: Using Precise MMIO Modeling for Effective Firmware Fuzzing
milestones.note: pushed firmware fuzzing toward precise MMIO hardware modeling for more effective, accurate bug-finding
